correctness.rationale: The semantics of value questions as constancy makes the inner implication exactly the functional dependency x→y. The inquisitive existential means a common z-value is omitted, so failing the outer implication is equivalent to an FD-consistent z-surjective subteam. A polynomial 2-CNF with one positive clause per z-fibre and pairwise exclusions for conflicting y-values proves the two-row algorithm even for arbitrary y-alphabets. A padded three-distinct-variable 3SAT reduction yields a pure equality domain, exactly three distinct triples per z-fibre, binary y, and equivalence SAT iff support failure, proving coNP-completeness. The bundled standard-library verifier expands the semantic connectives and passes 258 exhaustive tiny-domain teams, 97,336 exhaustive ternary two-fibre teams, 1,400 random 4-value teams and 5,180 CNF bridges. Finite checks supplement an explicit all-size proof.

value.rationale: The exact two-to-three row-size cutoff is a natural structural threshold for evaluating a fixed team-logic formula, with a substantive algorithm and hardness witness meeting the boundary. The equality-only presentation removes any need for an auxiliary clause-colouring predicate. The two-row algorithm works for all finite domains, so it is not an artefact of Boolean-valued data. These advances motivate bounded-choice team evaluation and cannot be described merely as a new notation, finite table or routine numerical increment. No claim is made of general InqBT or syntactic-optimality classifications.
